artists.biography: Peter Kenneth Frampton (born 22 April 1950) is an English born naturalized American musician, singer, songwriter, producer, guitarist and multi-instrumentalist. He was previously associated with the bands Humble Pie and The Herd. Frampton's international breakthrough album was his live release, Frampton Comes Alive!. The album sold over 6 million copies in the United States alone and spawned several hits. Since then he has released several major albums. He has also worked with David Bowie and both Matt Cameron and Mike McCready from Pearl Jam, among others. Frampton is best known for such hits as "Breaking All The Rules", "Show Me the Way", "Baby, I Love Your Way", "Do You Feel Like We Do", and "I'm in You", which remain staples on classic-rock radio. He has also appeared as himself in television shows such as The Simpsons and Family Guy. Frampton is known for his work as a guitar player and particularly with a Talkbox and his tenor voice.

perplexity.description:
Released in 1976 on A&M Records, Frampton Comes Alive! is a double live album by English rock musician Peter Frampton that captures the energy and musicianship of his 1975 US tour. The album blends classic rock, blues, and pop sensibilities, highlighted by Frampton’s signature use of the talkbox effect, which became a defining feature of his sound. Key tracks such as “Show Me the Way,” “Baby, I Love Your Way,” and the extended jam “Do You Feel Like We Do” showcase Frampton’s guitar prowess and engaging stage presence, making the album a quintessential example of 1970s live rock.

Frampton Comes Alive! marked a turning point in Peter Frampton’s career, following four studio albums with modest commercial success. The live album catapulted him to international stardom, becoming one of the best-selling live albums in history. It reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200, spending 10 non-consecutive weeks at the top and remaining on the charts for 97 weeks. Certified eight-times platinum in the US, the album was the best-selling of 1976 and is widely regarded as a landmark in rock music, praised for its dynamic performances and enduring influence on the live album format.
